newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE FRENCH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE FRENCH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Matches in the French first division this weekend:
(all kickoff times 1800 gmt, league position in parentheses)

Paris Saint-Germain (1) v Le Havre (15) Two successive draws have slowed PSG's progress and ended their run of eight clean sheets. Midfielder Laurent Fournier is back from suspension, but goalkeeper Bernard Lama is unfit after a cartilage operation.

Monaco (7) v Rennes (9) Monaco, dropped to seventh after defeat at Auxerre in midweek, and will be without injured Belgian Enzo Scifo, suspended midfielder Lilian Martin and John Collins, on World Cup duty with Scotland.

Caen (19) v Bordeaux (3) Bordeaux, who lost their unbeaten record at home to Strasbourg in midweek, will be without suspended defender Patrick Colleter and striker Jean-Pierre Papin, in the U.S. on private business.

Lens (12) v Metz (6) Czech striker Vladimir Smicer is back from injury to boost the morale of a Lens side who have slumped badly since their fine start of four wins in a row. Defender Rigobert Song is on international duty with Cameroon.

Nancy (20) v Lille (11) Bottom club Nancy, still looking for their first win, are without Northern Ireland international Phil Gray while French junior international Djezon Boutoille, who scored in Lille's 1-0 midweek win over Caen, is injured.

Cannes (10) v Auxerre (4) Goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier could return from injury for the champions, but their Algerian internationals Moussa Saib and Abdelhajid Tasfaout are away on African Nations Cup duty.

Guingamp (13) v Lyon (5) International duty has deprived Guingamp of defender Marek Jozwiak, who plays for Poland in their World Cup qualifier against England at Wembley on Wednesday, Liberian Christopher Wreh and Armenian Eric Assadourian.
Montpellier (17) v Bastia (2) Second-placed Bastia will be without striker Anton Drobnjak, with Yugoslavia for a World Cup qualifier on Sunday.
Nantes (18) v Nice (16) Struggling 1995 champions Nantes are unbeaten in three matches but still looking for first win of season. Argentine striker Javier Mazzoni faces late fitness test.

Strasbourg (14) V Marseille (8) Marseille travel without suspended Italian central defender Ivan Franceschini and three players on international duty: Germany's goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, Tony Cascarino of Ireland and Tunisian Medhi Ben Slimane.
